text:
maya: Quick smoke check — we saw a burst of ECC/Xid errors on gpu-rack-32 in eu-west-1 around 14:05 UTC, looks intermittent. Anyone oncall?
kevin: I'm around, digging in. initial alert was from grafana: `gpu_ecc_count{card=~".*"}` spike + eviction events.
bipin: saw the same in the telemetry feed, also noticed elevated `nv-hostengine` restarts. short bursts, ~30s each.
maya: timeline: 14:04 first ECC, 14:05 Xid 62, 14:06 drain triggered for instance i-0a...03, fallback to other region.
liz: do we have a panel that shows card-level intermittency score over time? the current healthscore is pretty static.
maya: not really, it's aggregated. proposal: add a 5m burst detector and a 'transient flake' band to the healthscore so we don't immediately escalate for 1-2 short bursts.
kevin: agree. current SLO fires on 1% card failures per hour, which flags a lot of noisy cards. suggestion: require either (a) sustained >1% over 30m OR (b) 3 discrete Xid/ECC bursts within 10m to mark as flaky.
bipin: we should also weight Xid62 differently than ECC_SINGLE_BIT — Xid62 is often driver/kernel transient, single-bit ECC can be tolerable depending on workload.
liz: can we capture kernel logs correlated to Xid timestamps in the grafana dashboard? even just a link to the last 200 lines from journald for the host.
maya: yes — we can add a log panel (loki) with a dashboard variable for host. small snippet for alert rule idea: 

```
ALERT FlakyCardBurst
  IF sum(increase(gpu_xid_count[5m])) by (card) >= 3
  FOR 5m
  LABELS {severity="warning"}
  ANNOTATIONS {summary="Card {{ $labels.card }} has 3+ XID bursts in 5m"}
```

kevin: also want a dampening policy so that first alert creates a paging action only if drain failed or we've hit replacement threshold. otherwise send to infra-runbook channel.
bipin: cost check: replacing a card vs. letting it run with retries — replacement (hardware ticket + cross-region migration) is ~3.5k USD per card and 6-12 hours. if the card is flaky but passes health checks 80% of time, it's cheaper to tolerate with routing fallback. need a TTL threshold to trigger replacement.
liz: agree. propose: replacement if (mean time between hard ECC errors < 72h) AND (fraction of heavy workloads impacted > 5%) over a 14d window.
maya: for SLOs — we want regional GPU availability 99.9% monthly for production pools. but we should expose per-card contribution to SLO so teams can choose to exclude flaky cards from strict SLAs.
kevin: implementation plan for dashboard changes: add a new grafana folder 'card-intermittency' with panels: 1) Xid/ECC burst heatmap (5m bins), 2) Card intermittency score (0-100) with transient band, 3) Kernel-restart annotation lane, 4) Cost-to-replace estimator (simple formula), 5) Alert history + runbook link.
bipin: intermittency score idea: combine burst rate (50%), post-drain failure rate (30%), and recovery latency (20%). normalize to 0-100 where >60 is flaky.
liz: can we have a synthetic check that runs a tiny compute kernel on card for 10s at low priority and monitors Xid/ECC during the run? run every 2h for candidate cards.
kevin: yes but careful with production load. run on canary instances or during low-util windows. add to dedicated pool jobs.
maya: on grafana alert tuning, let's add a 'grace window' label so Ops tickets don't get created for transient noise. Example flow: Warning -> post to #infra-runbook -> if persists 30m escalate to #oncall-pager.
bipin: also implement cardiac-sampling: sample 10% of requests to all cards and check for p50/p95 latency spikes correlated with card id. helps catch silent degradation that ECC counters miss.
liz: good. UI question: can we add a per-region toggle to the health algorithm so ap-south and eu-west have different weightings? their typical error profiles differ.
kevin: yep, make weights editable in the dashboard JSON model — region overrides.
maya: someone take the patch for grafana panels and alert rules? I can own the runbook updates.
kevin: I'll draft the prometheus alert and grafana JSON. aiming for PR by EOD. cc @sre-bot to post the new alert to staging for 24h.
sre-bot: scheduled job created: deploy alert to staging (namespace=staging, group=eng-runtime) at 16:30 UTC. monitor window 24h.
bipin: FYI I'll run a replacement-cost sim on Friday to see break-even points for replacement vs. routing for different workload mixes.
liz: small follow-ups: add a panel that surfaces top-5 affected customer routes when a card shows intermittent errors, and a direct link to trigger temporary exclusion from routing for a card (safety-guarded).
maya: agreed. Also add a metric for 'time-to-fallback' — how long between initial error and successful request routed to fallback model/region. want < 2s target.
kevin: last note: let's ensure the alert has runbook links and the playbook suggests soft-restart (NVidia hostengine), evict-if-still-followed-by-two-drains, then crate hardware ticket.
maya: perfect. I'll put the proposed SLO adjustments and the new dashboard mock in the drive. thanks team :thumbsup:
kevin: thanks, rolling this into a staging deploy now.
liz: will test the kernel-log panel with a host variable.
bipin: will upload the cost sim results Friday.
maya: closing loop — we'll reconvene next week after 24h staging smoke results.
